title: A study to compare a new study medicine, ABP 938 8 mg with EYLEA® HD (aflibercept 8 mg) in participants with Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration.
official: A Randomized, Double-masked, Comparative Clinical Study Evaluating the Efficacy, Safety, and Immunogenicity of ABP 938 8 mg Versus EYLEA® HD (Aflibercept) Delivered via Intravitreal Injection in Participants with Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate similarity in efficacy between ABP 938 8 mg and aflibercept XXX 8 mg by evaluating the change in BCVA
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 01 Men or women ≥ 50 years old, capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Appendix 1, Section 10.1.3 which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF) and in this study protocol
2. 02 Active, treatment-naïve subfoveal CNV lesions secondary to nAMD including juxtafoveal lesions that affect the fovea as confirmed by spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and fluorescein angiography (FA) in the SE (fundus photography [FP] to be used for documentation)
3. 03 Total area of CNV (including both classic and occult components) > 50% of the total lesion area in the SE
4. 04 The BCVA letter score ≥ 24 and ≤ 78 letters, in the SE
5. 05 Presence of intra and/or subretinal fluid affecting the central subfield of the SE as identified by SD-OCT attributable to active CNV. The central subfield is defined as a circle with a diameter of 1 mm, centered on the fovea.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 01 Total lesion size > 12 disc areas (30.5 mm2) including blood, scars, and neovascularization, as assessed by FA in the SE
2. 10 History of retinal detachment in the SE
3. 11 History of macular hole of stage ≥ 2 in the SE
4. 12 Any macular pathology that might limit vision, ie, vitreomacular traction or significant epiretinal membrane in the SE
5. 13 Any intraocular or periocular surgery ≤ 12 weeks (84 days) before randomization on the SE, except lid surgery, which may not have taken place ≤ 4 weeks (28 days) before randomization, as long as it is unlikely to interfere with the injection
6. 14 History of, or likely future need of, tube shunt surgery, trabeculectomy, or other filtration surgery in the SE
7. 15 Uncontrolled glaucoma (defined as IOP ≥ 25 mmHg despite treatment with antiglaucoma medication) in the SE
8. 16 Aphakia or pseudophakia with complete absence of posterior capsule (unless it occurred as a result of a yttrium aluminum garnet [YAG] posterior capsulotomy, performed > 30 days before screening) in the SE
9. 17 Previous therapeutic radiation in the region of the SE
10. 18 History of corneal transplant or corneal dystrophy in the SE
11. 19 Significant media opacities, including cataract, which might interfere with visual acuity or assessment of safety and efficacy, in the SE
12. 02 Scar, fibrosis, or atrophy involving the central subfield in the SE
13. 20 History of irregular astigmatism or amblyopia with chronic limitation of BCVA in the SE
14. 21 Any concurrent intraocular condition other than nAMD in the SE that, in the opinion of the investigator, requires planned medical or surgical intervention during the study or increases the risk to the participant beyond what is expected from standard procedures of intraocular injection, or which otherwise may interfere with the injection procedure or with evaluation of efficacy or safety
15. 22 History or clinical evidence of DR, DME, idiopathic autoimmune uveitis, or any other vascular disease affecting the retina, other than nAMD
16. 23 Evidence of active extraocular or periocular infection or inflammation (including infectious blepharitis, keratitis, scleritis, or conjunctivitis) in either eye at the time of screening or randomization
17. 24 Any intraocular inflammation/infection in either eye ≤ 12 weeks (84 days) of the randomization
18. 25 Active scleritis or episcleritis or presence of scleromalacia
19. 26 Only 1 functional eye (eg, BCVA of counting fingers or less in the eye with worse vision) or ocular conditions with poorer prognosis in the FE
20. 27 Active systemic infections or a history of infections meeting the following criteria: a. any active infection for which systemic anti-infectives were used ≤ 4 weeks (28 days) prior to randomization; b. recurrent or chronic infections that, in the opinion of the investigator, could compromise the participant’s safety or study integrity
21. 28 Uncontrolled BP (defined as systolic ≥ 160 mmHg or diastolic ≥ 95 mmHg). Participants may be treated with up to 3 anti-hypertensive medications to achieve adequate BP control. Blood pressure needs to be stable for at least 12 weeks (84 days) prior to screening
22. 29 Cerebrovascular event of myocardial infarction ≤ 24 weeks (168 days) prior to screening
23. 03 Scar or fibrosis involving > 50% of the total lesion in the SE
24. 30 Renal insufficiency requiring dialysis, or renal transplant at screening or likely during the study
25. 31 Any contraindications indicated in the locally approved prescribing information (label) for aflibercept
26. 32 Uncontrolled, clinically significant systemic disease such as diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, including moderate to severe heart failure (New York Heart Association class III/IV), renal disease, or liver disease that might affect interpretation of the results of the study, or renders the participant at high risk for treatment complications
27. 33 Malignancy ≤ 5 years EXCEPT treated and considered cured cutaneous squamous or basal cell carcinoma, in situ cervical cancer, OR in situ breast ductal carcinoma
28. 34 History or evidence of any other clinically significant disorder, condition, disease or clinical laboratory abnormality that, in the opinion of the investigator or study medical monitor, if consulted, would pose a risk to participant safety or interfere with the study evaluation or results interpretation
29. 35 Any prior or concomitant ocular or systemic treatment (with an investigational or approved, anti-VEGF or anti-VEGF/anti-angiopoietin agent) in the SE, or surgery for nAMD in the SE, except dietary supplements or vitamins
30. 36 Long-acting steroids, either systemically or intraocularly in the SE ≤ 16 weeks (112 days) before the screening visit or any treatment with IVT implant, gene therapy, or cell therapy in the SE at any time
31. 37 Intramuscular or intravenous corticosteroids ≤ 4 weeks (28 days) before randomization
32. 38 Vitreoretinal surgery and/or including scleral buckling at any time in the SE
33. 39 Ocriplasmin (JETREA®) at any time in the SE
34. 04 Subretinal hemorrhage involving > 50% of the total lesion area, or if the blood under the fovea ≥ 1 disc areas in size in the SE
35. 40 Any other intraocular surgery or panretinal laser photocoagulation or macular laser photocoagulation in the SE ≤ 12 weeks (84 days) before the screening visit
36. 41 YAG capsulotomy in the SE ≤ 30 days before the screening visit
37. 42 Prior treatment of the FE with investigational therapy (eg, with anti-angiopoietin/anti-VEGF bispecific monoclonal antibodies) ≤ 180 days before the screening visit or IVT implant, gene therapy, or cell therapy at any time. Note: Prior treatment in the FE with approved anti-VEGF therapy is permitted in this study. Additionally, treatment with bevacizumab in the FE is allowed if it is considered standard care in some countries or institutions
38. 43 Prior systemic anti-VEGF treatment ≤ 24 weeks (168 days) before screening visit
39. 44 Aflibercept IVT injection during screening period in the FE
40. 45 Participation in other clinical studies requiring administration of investigational treatments (other than vitamins and minerals) at the time of screening, or ≤ 30 days or 5 half-lives of administration of the previous investigational product, whichever is longer. Other investigational procedures while participating in this study are excluded.
41. 46 For women of childbearing potential: pregnant or breast feeding, planning to become pregnant, or not agreeing to use a highly effective method of contraception (eg, true abstinence, sterilization, birth control pills, Depo Provera injections, contraceptive implants, or other effective methods) while enrolled in the study and for 4 months after the last dose of investigational product
42. 47 Sexually active male participants and their partners who are of childbearing potential (ie, neither surgically sterile nor postmenopausal) and not agreeing to use  highly effective method of contraception (eg, true abstinence, sterilization, birth control pills, Depo Provera injections, contraceptive implants, or other effective methods) while on study and for 3 months after the last dose of investigational product. Male participants must agree not to donate sperm during study and for 3 months following treatment with test article or until the scheduled EoS (whichever is longer)
43. 48 Allergy or hypersensitivity to investigational product, to any of the excipients of ABP 938 8 mg or aflibercept XXX 8 mg, or to other study-related procedures/medications (eg, anesthesia, antiseptic, fluorescein dye)
44. 49 Participant likely to not be available to complete all protocol-required study visits or procedures, and/or to comply with all required study procedures to the best of the participant and investigator’s knowledge
45. 05 Pigment epithelial detachment in the SE > 400 μm, as determined by SD-OCT
46. 50 Participant is a member of the clinical site study team and/or his/her immediate family
47. 06 Presence of retinal pigment epithelium tears or rips involving the macula in the SE
48. 07 History of any vitreous hemorrhage ≤ 4 weeks (28 days) before randomization in the SE
49. 08 Presence of other causes of CNV, including pathologic myopia (spherical equivalent ≥ 8 diopters negative or axial length ≥ 25 mm), ocular histoplasmosis syndrome, angioid streaks, choroidal rupture, or multifocal choroiditis in the SE
50. 09 Prior vitrectomy or laser surgery of the macula (including photodynamic therapy or focal laser photocoagulation) in the SE
